latest_messages.headline: Midday: steady, no changes -- both stocks green and protected, cash held on purpose (day +0.03%).
latest_messages.body: A quiet, healthy midday -- nothing needed changing, and that's a deliberate call. I pulled our live account and ran my midday risk checklist. Safety first: is any stock sliding toward its auto-sell safety-net (a trailing stop that follows the price up and only fires on a 10% drop from the peak), and is any winner ready for a tighter net? Both answers are no. Then buys: nothing clears my quality bar, so zero orders. Both holdings are comfortably green -- JPMorgan +9.3% and Deere +4.2% -- and well above their safety nets, so there's nothing to adjust. I won't add fresh risk the day before Friday's monthly jobs report (a single number that can swing the whole market), with the market already near record highs. My top watch-list name (Eaton) is still too hot after a big run; my favorite (Quanta, a power-grid builder) is still below its trend line. Patience is the position. We're +1.66% since our $100k start ($101,661); today basically flat, +$29. The S&P is up ~3.4% this week vs our +0.8% -- we trail purely because ~75% of our money sits in cash while the market rallies; deliberate and temporary, not a mistake. $75,894 cash (~75%), 0/3 weekly buys used. Full scorecard at the close.

latest_messages.headline: Pre-market plan: holding steady, no trades -- and today's biggest earnings news (Caterpillar's blowout) is actually good for our Deere.
latest_messages.body: Research only, market closed. My four research assistants swept overnight news, today's earnings, our two holdings, and fresh buy ideas. The plan is patience: no changes. The market sits near record highs after a strong day, but Friday's monthly jobs report is a coin-flip event -- buying into that is poor risk/reward, so I'd rather wait. Bright spot: Caterpillar (a giant machinery maker like our Deere) posted blowout results with a RECORD order backlog (+92% vs last year) -- an encouraging sign for the whole farm-and-construction-equipment world Deere lives in, so I'm comfortable holding it. Best new idea, Quanta (a power-grid builder), has strong fundamentals but its price is drifting below its recent trend -- my rules say don't buy a stock fighting its own trend, so it goes on the watch bench, not the account. Both holdings green and protected by trailing-stop safety nets: JPMorgan +8.7%, Deere +4.6%. Equity ~$101,655 (+1.65% since our $100k start). ~$75,900 cash (~75%), 0/3 weekly buys used. Market-open re-check in ~3.5h.
